text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No privacy or generative AI review recorded","detail":"The proposal uses an LLM (generative AI) on drivers' GPS location history, which is personal data, to draft performance warnings that affect drivers. The only review noted is 'Ops leadership supports the pilot', which is not a privacy, legal, or AI policy review.","evidence_quote":"Ops leadership supports the pilot.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record privacy/data protection review, generative AI policy review, and HR/legal review of the warning process before launch."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days of standard and only 4 weeks for a 12-week target","detail":"The plan randomizes by market with only a few markets likely, so power at the stated MDE is doubtful and no clustering is addressed. A 4-week duration also cannot evidence a target defined over 12 weeks. Note that 4 weeks meets the 14-day minimum, but the mismatch with the 12-week target and the cluster-level power are unaddressed.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by market. Duration: 4 weeks. MDE: 0.3 incidents per 10,000 trips, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align the duration with the 12-week measurement window, state the number of markets, and compute power accounting for market-level clustering."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for driver-impacting warnings","detail":"The change affects driver discipline and could affect driver retention, delivery quality, and fairness, yet the only guardrail is earnings. There are no guardrails for driver attrition/churn, on-time delivery or delivery success, warning accuracy/error rate, or disparate impact across driver groups.","evidence_quote":"Driver Hourly Earnings: must not fall below baseline.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as driver churn/attrition, on-time delivery rate, warning dispute/overturn rate, and fairness across driver segments."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Time-savings problem claim has no quantification or verifiable source","detail":"The claim that managers spend 'hours' drafting warnings is cited only to an unspecified ops time study, with no figures or link. The problem's magnitude cannot be verified.","evidence_quote":"Operations managers spend hours drafting warnings to drivers with repeated service issues (source: LMD ops time study).","citations":[],"recommendation":"Provide the time study's figures and a link or document reference, and quantify the time spent per warning."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric does not match the intervention's purpose","detail":"The stated problem is manager time spent drafting warnings, but the success metric is Driver Safety Incident Rate, with no causal link and no metric for drafting time or warning quality. It is unclear how LLM-drafted warnings would reduce safety incidents.","evidence_quote":"Driver Safety Incident Rate: baseline 3.1 per 10,000 trips, target 2.6 within 12 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add a metric for manager drafting time and warning quality, and justify the causal pathway to safety incident rate, or drop the unrelated metric."}]}
